## Structure

### Header / Navbar

The Figma header was a fully custom block. The build uses a standard navbar with dropdowns on
desktop and an offcanvas drawer on mobile — no manual JS. See [Navbar](/docs/2026/components/navbar)
for the full breakdown.

### Hero

Two columns, image on one side, heading/lead/CTA on the other, vertically centered.

### Accordion — What to expect

Responsive: on mobile it is a collapsible accordion; above `sm` it becomes three cards side by
side (via a SCSS media query). Multiple panels can stay open at once — see
[Accordion](/docs/2026/components/accordion).

### News cards

A responsive card grid, three columns at its widest. Each card uses `.card.news-card.h-100` —
the card base provides `display: flex; flex-direction: column`, so the "Read more" link stays
pinned to the bottom with `mt-auto`. See [Cards](/docs/2026/components/cards).

The event's visual identity — the sticker shadows, animated underlines, badge treatment,
decorative media frames, and accordion/sponsor/avatar styling — is hand-built and genuinely
custom; none of it comes from off-the-shelf utility classes.

## Accessibility

- Skip link: `.visually-hidden-focusable` (replaces the custom `.skip-link`)
- `aria-labelledby` on every `<section>` with a matching `id` on the heading
- `aria-hidden="true"` on all decorative SVGs
- `aria-current="page"` on the active item in the mobile drawer
- `aria-expanded` managed automatically by the site's interactive behavior (dropdown, collapse,
  offcanvas)
